subject.title: [Bug] WebChat: optimistic USER messages are lost (not just hidden) when chat.send returns before the durable transcript lands — full-replace history reconcile drops them

question: Should WebChat `chat.send` only return `started` after the user turn is durably visible/progressing, or should OpenClaw keep the current nonblocking ACK and add a visible failure/retry contract for missed persistence?
rationale: This changes the public send-success boundary and can affect latency, duplicate suppression, session rollover, and runtime-owned transcript persistence, so an automated repair lane should not choose the contract unilaterally.

options.title: Require durable/progress-bound ACK
options.body: Treat `started` as a guarantee that the user turn is durably visible or has an established recorder/runtime persistence path before returning success.

options.title: Keep nonblocking ACK with visible recovery
options.body: Keep the fast ACK behavior but require a visible error/retry/audit path whenever the turn cannot be persisted or dispatched after acceptance.

options.title: Port the candidate PR through current recorder boundaries
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80670 as source work only after it is rebased and aligned with the current shared user-turn recorder/session-accessor boundary.

recommendation.title: Require durable/progress-bound ACK
recommendation.body: Treat `started` as a guarantee that the user turn is durably visible or has an established recorder/runtime persistence path before returning success.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision centers on the shared user-turn transcript recorder and persistence boundary they recently authored.
